findings.title: The serial output cap (64 GiB = 68.72 GB) sits exactly at the 0181 floor, with thin margin on the U path
findings.evidence: CAPS_FIRST_NGC_POINT_C2V001 output_cap_bytes 68719476736, basis '37-41.5 GB at I = 16 before route B and the readout'. Claude3's own RI45-12 verifier record REVIEW_RI45_12_RESULT_C3V001.txt (cc25da63, L214): 'With route-B node logs (about 1.13 GB per route-B prepare) the U total is about 50-60 GB or more, so ... at least 64 GiB (68.7 GB) leaves thin margin. findings.title: Memory-gate reserve units: the 27 GB campaign reserve is a GiB figure, so the gate thresholds are about 2.1 GB lax

Watch v002 3862b645 L14 computes each per-run value as KiB/1048576, which is GiB, so 27.1 GiB = 29.10 GB. CAPS memory_gate and README 5 use 103 - 27 - peaks in decimal GB: 55.9 / 26.0 / 8.7 (8.79) GB. In consistent units they are 53.8 / 23.9 / 6.7 GB. The object already flags the watch's GiB label (watch_units), but not that the reserve itself comes from that label. When root fixes the watch units (README 7 item 5), the reserve should become 29.1 GB.

findings.title: Comparator tokens depend on --serial/--twin being spelled exactly like the --outdir given to root_monitor
findings.evidence: compare_identity_pair_c2v001 Side.tok replaces only the given run path and its realpath (L152-166). The driver writes request.json argv from os.path.abspath(outdir), unresolved (driver L8990-8991, ctx.request). The binding sets numerical_controls.uv_tail = controller.identity(), whose 'sidecar' is the argv path, also unresolved (binding L144; controller L291-296). The worker records resolved paths. runs_ext is a link to External1 (0184 L3). If root passes the resolved form, the argv and sidecar spellings are not tokenized, and an honest pair reads DIFFERENT (a false DIFFERENT). That is the safe direction: everything stays serial, and the compare can be re-run to a new --out. Rule: pass the identical outdir strings, or tokenize the abspath forms too.

findings.title: The twin's planned stop and the pair memory window both rely on root's N4 early kill
findings.evidence: From the RI45-12 verifier figures (N8 tree 31,455 s E; replica 7,135 / 11,371 s; serial side 17,750 / 26,184 s): unless killed, the twin at E runs about 9 more iterations (about 1,737 s each) to its 22,752 s wall cap. That is about 25-29 GB of output at 2.3-2.6 GB per iteration, approaching its 32 GiB output cap. The serial at E passes the end of its iteration 1 at 17,750 s while the twin is still alive, outside the 'serial_iterations_0_1_spike' the pair gate (26.0 / 8.7 GB) assumes. README 7 item 3 names only a WALL_CAP stop as planned. Root's N4 (kill the twin once iteration_000{N-1}/COMPLETED.json and the sidecar iteration record exist; any twin cap stop is planned) closes both, and should be the ruling.

corrections: L4 arithmetic (FORMAL; class and conclusion unchanged). The lens divided the whole N8 tree (31,455 s at E) by 14 iterations, giving 1,737 s per iteration, 'about 9 more iterations' and '25-29 GB, approaching its 32 GiB output cap'. But that tree includes the readout, which stays serial in the parent (10,427 s at E), and stage 02 (3,209 s at E), and E assumes I = 7. So the twin's route-A iterations at E take about 17,800 s in all, about 2,100 s each after the 7,135 s replica point. At E the twin finishes route A near 17,800 s and is in its readout when the 22,752 s cap fires, with about 16-18 GB written. If route A ran 16 iterations at E pace, it would be about 9 iterations and 21-23 GB. At U it is about 5.5 iterations and 14 GB. In no case is the 34.36 GB twin output cap approached. What still holds: at E the twin is alive past the serial's iteration 1 (17,750 s), so the planned stop and the pair memory window both need root's N4 kill.

L1 consequence understated (FORMAL; still a NOTE). A133 3(c) reruns the identical spec with only the RSS cap (raised to RAM) and the wall cap (doubled) relaxed; the output cap stays the same. So an honest run that crosses 64 GiB stops at the same point on the rerun, and two identical non-INFRA stops mark the call invalid, leaving the member unevaluated under 3(f). This is worse than 'a full rerun'. Root's cap ruling should set the output cap (about 96 GiB, or a cap measured at iterations 0-1) and say how an OUTPUT_CAP stop is treated under 3(c). It stays a NOTE because no honest estimate exceeds 68.7 GB (the RI45-12 verifier gives about 50-60 GB 'or more'; I did not count the route-B prepares).
